Good afternoon, and welcome to the market. Here is the information for today, Saturday. We are open until six o'clock, and after five o'clock everything in the fruit section is half price. The shop on the corner has a sale this week: all the winter jackets are thirty percent off, so a jacket that is two hundred is one hundred and forty today. Two things, please. First, many of our small shops do not take cards, only cash, so please ask before you choose. Second, if you buy something and you want to change it later, you need the receipt. No receipt, no change. Thank you, and have a good afternoon.

Hi, it's me. You are going to laugh. I went to that shop you told me about, the one on Market Street. I wanted one thing, only one, and I came home with three. So, the jacket. It was two hundred and twenty, which is too expensive for a jacket, but it was thirty percent off, so I paid one hundred and fifty four. That is not bad. Then I saw a small bag for forty, and a scarf for eighteen. The man at the counter was very nice and he gave me the receipt for everything, because I told him I am not sure about the scarf. Anyway. I have no money now, and it is Tuesday. Call me later.
Excuse me, how much is this? Two hundred? That is a little expensive for me. Do you have a smaller size? I will take it, thank you. Can I have the receipt, please?
